title: Favorite clarinetists: George Lewis, George Boyd and a tall brown-skinned player
summary: Watts names George Lewis and George Boyd, played a few jobs with Lewis in 1945, and cannot recall a tall clarinetist in the Eureka.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Who were the great clarinetists? Favorites and rivals

blocks.x: Who was your favorite clarinet player back in those days? Did you have a favorite? Oh yeah.
Well I'll tell you, my favorite clarinet player is, he's around here right now, and that's George. Lewis.
Who was he with in those times?

Well I don't know. George would look like he was freelancing, you know. He'd play with, you know, just so many of them, but he was always so popular, so busy, you know. Yeah. He had another tall brownskin fellow, I don't know his name. He played fine clarinet for brass band work. But George Lewis, see I made a couple of jobs with him years ago, see, playing at a hall, a ballroom, see, back on the main street between Claiborne and, what is that? San Jacinto. San Jacinto. Yeah, I had the privilege of playing with George Lewis. He hired me with his little combo, see. Now that was, that was before I left New Orleans, that was in 45, see, when I was home visiting my people. When I stayed here that year, you know, after I got out of the army, I made a couple of jobs with George Lewis back there. But to sit down and listen at clarinet players, I tell you that old George Lewis, man, he used to, I mean, old George Lewis from back there with that old bad cough, that strong cough, it sounded like his lungs coming out, no blood or nothing. He used to blow a lot of clarinet. Who's this? Old George Lewis. George Lewis, the one that's living now, yeah. No, no.
George A. Boyd, that's who I mean. Yeah, yeah, yeah. Yeah, not George Lewis, George A. Boyd.
So you liked both of them, huh?
I wonder who the tall, brown-skinned boy in the street was that you heard on clarinet that was good?
I don't know, I might know his name, but I can't. Who did he play with?

Oh, he played with the Eureka, played a while with the Eureka. And in 55 when I come here with Anderson, he played for the Buzzy with us, he was Anderson's clarinet player. Yeah. And I can't think of that fella's name, tall fella, brown-skinned, and blows a lot of clarinet. No E-flat, B-flat. You use that B-flat.
The only one I can think of maybe is Brother Cornbread or something like that, but that doesn't sound right. No, I can't remember.
I have to look it up.
I have to look it up. Yeah, good problem to have it. Somewhat. Because he's one of the old side men, he's really one of the old druner here. And I haven't seen him this year, I don't know maybe.
